## godot_engine_source_build

<pre>
load("@autoload_rules_godot//godot/engine:repositories.bzl", "godot_engine_source_build")

godot_engine_source_build(<a href="#godot_engine_source_build-name">name</a>, <a href="#godot_engine_source_build-source">source</a>, <a href="#godot_engine_source_build-platforms">platforms</a>, <a href="#godot_engine_source_build-cpus">cpus</a>, <a href="#godot_engine_source_build-build_targets">build_targets</a>, <a href="#godot_engine_source_build-ios_environments">ios_environments</a>,
                          <a href="#godot_engine_source_build-enabled_modules">enabled_modules</a>, <a href="#godot_engine_source_build-custom_modules">custom_modules</a>, <a href="#godot_engine_source_build-patches">patches</a>, <a href="#godot_engine_source_build-patch_strip">patch_strip</a>, <a href="#godot_engine_source_build-build_options">build_options</a>,
                          <a href="#godot_engine_source_build-build_name">build_name</a>, <a href="#godot_engine_source_build-python">python</a>, <a href="#godot_engine_source_build-configure_timeout">configure_timeout</a>, <a href="#godot_engine_source_build-lock_file">lock_file</a>, <a href="#godot_engine_source_build-engine">engine</a>)
</pre>

Declare a source build: its source recipes and its hub, from a module extension.

Call during a module extension's implementation; the helper declares repositories and
cannot run in BUILD files. It applies one build policy to the valid rows its filters
select: one godot_engine_build per row, named `<name>_<platform>_<cpu>[_<environment>]_<build_target>`,
for Android one godot_android_shell named `<name>_android_shell` with the same patches,
and the hub `<name>` with one component per slot in `@<name>//toolchains`, registered
through `@<name>//toolchains:all`. Common inputs apply to every row; declaring the
source build configures no recipe until a build requests its payload.

Example (an extension implementation):
```starlark
godot_engine_source_build(
    name = "godot_source_build",
    source = "@godot_sources//:source.json",
    platforms = ["macos", "ios"],
    build_targets = ["editor", "template_release"],
)
```

## godot_android_shell

<pre>
load("@autoload_rules_godot//godot/engine:repositories.bzl", "godot_android_shell")

godot_android_shell(<a href="#godot_android_shell-name">name</a>, <a href="#godot_android_shell-patch_strip">patch_strip</a>, <a href="#godot_android_shell-patches">patches</a>, <a href="#godot_android_shell-source">source</a>)
</pre>

Build Godot's Java/Kotlin Android shell library from a source descriptor.

Call through use_repo_rule in MODULE.bazel, or from a module extension. The
repository extracts the source, applies the patches and exposes `:debug` and
`:release`, the Android shell library of each template variant built with rules_android and
rules_kotlin; their `.aar` outputs, such as `:release.aar`, are godot_android_runtime
shells. Java and Kotlin target Godot's language level per target, so no Kotlin
toolchain is registered. The shell library's Maven dependencies come from autoload_rules_godot's
contribution to the shared `maven` repository; repin after adding autoload_rules_godot.

Example (MODULE.bazel):
```starlark
godot_android_shell = use_repo_rule(
    "@autoload_rules_godot//godot/engine:repositories.bzl", "godot_android_shell",
)
godot_android_shell(name = "godot_shell", source = "@godot_sources//:source.json")
```

| repository | none | always | repository creation; generated entrypoints described above |

none

## godot_editor_archive

<pre>
load("@autoload_rules_godot//godot/engine:repositories.bzl", "godot_editor_archive")

godot_editor_archive(<a href="#godot_editor_archive-name">name</a>, <a href="#godot_editor_archive-binary">binary</a>, <a href="#godot_editor_archive-integrity">integrity</a>, <a href="#godot_editor_archive-urls">urls</a>, <a href="#godot_editor_archive-version">version</a>)
</pre>

Acquire one checksum-pinned prebuilt editor archive.

Call from a module extension or through use_repo_rule. The repository exposes
`:editor`, the executable with the complete distribution as runfiles, for a
godot_editor_component; it registers nothing. The editor must match the operating
system and CPU of the execution platform of the slot it fills. The declared
version is checked for ruleset support; it is not read from the archive.
godot_engines.prebuilt uses this rule for catalogued releases.

Example (MODULE.bazel; replace URL and digest with a real pinned archive):
```starlark
godot_editor_archive = use_repo_rule(
    "@autoload_rules_godot//godot/engine:repositories.bzl",
    "godot_editor_archive",
)
godot_editor_archive(
    name = "godot_editor_custom",
    urls = ["https://example.com/godot-editor.zip"],
    integrity = "sha256-<base64-digest>",
    binary = "Godot.app/Contents/MacOS/Godot",
    version = "4.7.2",
)
```

### Default outputs
| kind | cardinality | availability | behavior |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| repository | none | always | repository creation; generated entrypoints described above |

none

| @{repository}//:distribution | files | operation | consume the complete editor distribution | public | false | repository acquired | always |

## godot_engine_build

<pre>
load("@autoload_rules_godot//godot/engine:repositories.bzl", "godot_engine_build")

godot_engine_build(<a href="#godot_engine_build-name">name</a>, <a href="#godot_engine_build-build_name">build_name</a>, <a href="#godot_engine_build-build_options">build_options</a>, <a href="#godot_engine_build-build_target">build_target</a>, <a href="#godot_engine_build-configure_timeout">configure_timeout</a>, <a href="#godot_engine_build-cpu">cpu</a>,
                   <a href="#godot_engine_build-custom_modules">custom_modules</a>, <a href="#godot_engine_build-enabled_modules">enabled_modules</a>, <a href="#godot_engine_build-environment">environment</a>, <a href="#godot_engine_build-lock_file">lock_file</a>, <a href="#godot_engine_build-lock_key">lock_key</a>, <a href="#godot_engine_build-patch_strip">patch_strip</a>,
                   <a href="#godot_engine_build-patches">patches</a>, <a href="#godot_engine_build-platform">platform</a>, <a href="#godot_engine_build-python">python</a>, <a href="#godot_engine_build-repin">repin</a>, <a href="#godot_engine_build-source">source</a>)
</pre>

Configure one fixed Godot source recipe and emit granular rules_cc build targets.

Call through use_repo_rule in MODULE.bazel, or from a module extension. The recipe
extracts the archive of a godot_engine_source descriptor into its own repository,
applies the patches, adds the modules and captures the upstream build graph; SCons
never compiles. Compilation runs later as Bazel actions, only for the outputs a build
requests. The recipe registers nothing: name its outputs as component payloads.
Fetching needs host Python 3.9+ (or the python attribute), patch when patches are
supplied, and the target operating system's SDK. Bazel's repo contents cache, local
or remote (--experimental_remote_repo_contents_cache), reuses Android, iOS and macOS
recipes; Linux recipes configure on every host, because Godot enables Linux features
by the packages installed there.

Example (MODULE.bazel):
```starlark
godot_engine_build = use_repo_rule(
    "@autoload_rules_godot//godot/engine:repositories.bzl", "godot_engine_build",
)
godot_engine_build(
    name = "godot_macos_arm64_release",
    cpu = "arm64",
    build_target = "template_release",
    platform = "macos",
    source = "@godot_sources//:source.json",
)
```

A source contradicting the descriptor's version, unknown or rules_godot-controlled
options, unresolvable modules and rejected patch hunks fail the recipe. See
[source-built engines](../../engine.md) for custom modules, options and patches.

## godot_engine_source

<pre>
load("@autoload_rules_godot//godot/engine:repositories.bzl", "godot_engine_source")

godot_engine_source(<a href="#godot_engine_source-name">name</a>, <a href="#godot_engine_source-sha256">sha256</a>, <a href="#godot_engine_source-strip_prefix">strip_prefix</a>, <a href="#godot_engine_source-urls">urls</a>, <a href="#godot_engine_source-version">version</a>)
</pre>

Acquire one immutable Godot source archive for godot_engine_build recipes.

Call through use_repo_rule in MODULE.bazel, or from a module extension. The
repository exports `:source.json`, the descriptor recipes take as `source`, and the
archive itself; it never extracts or configures the sources. Upstream releases and
fork archives alike are pinned by digest and their canonical Godot version, which
every recipe checks against the extracted version.py.

Example (MODULE.bazel):
```starlark
godot_engine_source = use_repo_rule(
    "@autoload_rules_godot//godot/engine:repositories.bzl", "godot_engine_source",
)
godot_engine_source(
    name = "godot_sources",
    sha256 = "e954996374cbd1cb5d72e0e3781cc537408e6ce73b010b12c6c2f308a820690a",
    strip_prefix = "godot-4.7.2-stable",
    urls = ["https://github.com/godotengine/godot/archive/refs/tags/4.7.2-stable.tar.gz"],
    version = "4.7.2",
)
```

### Default outputs
| kind | cardinality | availability | behavior |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| repository | none | always | repository creation; generated entrypoints described above |

### Output groups
none

| @{repository}//:source.json | files | operation | the source descriptor godot_engine_build recipes take as source | public | false | archive acquired | always |
| @{repository}//:{archive} | files | operation | the acquired archive, which recipes extract independently | public | false | archive acquired | always |

none

## godot_export_templates_archive

<pre>
load("@autoload_rules_godot//godot/engine:repositories.bzl", "godot_export_templates_archive")

godot_export_templates_archive(<a href="#godot_export_templates_archive-name">name</a>, <a href="#godot_export_templates_archive-integrity">integrity</a>, <a href="#godot_export_templates_archive-linux_cpus">linux_cpus</a>, <a href="#godot_export_templates_archive-macos_cpus">macos_cpus</a>, <a href="#godot_export_templates_archive-urls">urls</a>, <a href="#godot_export_templates_archive-version">version</a>)
</pre>

Acquire one checksum-pinned export-template archive.

Call from a module extension or through use_repo_rule. The repository exposes one
runtime target per desktop operating system, CPU and template variant,
such as `:linux_x86_64_release` or `:macos_debug`, each carrying GodotRuntimeInfo,
for godot_runtime_component payloads. Coverage follows the archive contents: an
archive without a debug template omits the debug target, and macos_cpus
describes its macOS layout. An archive with iOS templates also exposes `:ios_debug`
and `:ios_release`, XCFramework imports with the dependent frameworks the
archive carries; they serve device and simulator slots alike. Downloading happens
only when a payload is requested. godot_engines.prebuilt uses this rule for
catalogued releases.

Example (MODULE.bazel; replace URL and digest with a real pinned archive):
```starlark
godot_export_templates_archive = use_repo_rule(
    "@autoload_rules_godot//godot/engine:repositories.bzl",
    "godot_export_templates_archive",
)
godot_export_templates_archive(
    name = "godot_templates_custom",
    urls = ["https://example.com/export_templates.tpz"],
    integrity = "sha512-<base64-digest>",
    version = "4.7.2",
)
```

### Default outputs
| kind | cardinality | availability | behavior |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| repository | none | always | repository creation; generated entrypoints described above |

none
